make.name: Citroën
make.description: French car maker founded by André Citroën in 1919, part of PSA from 1976 and of Stellantis since 2021. Its electric cars started with the Mitsubishi-built C-Zero in 2010; today it sells the Ami quadricycle, the low-cost ë-C3 and ë-C3 Aircross, the ë-C4 and ë-C4 X, the ë-C5 Aircross and electric Berlingo and SpaceTourer people carriers.

models.name: Ami
models.description: Two-seat electric quadricycle (L6e, limited to 45 km/h) built in Kenitra, Morocco since 2020, with a 5.5 kWh battery and a 6 kW motor. It can be driven in France without a full licence. A facelift with a new front and rear was shown in October 2024. Opel sells a twin as the Rocks Electric and Fiat a restyled twin as the Topolino.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launched in 2020 after the 2019 Ami One concept; symmetrical body with the old double-chevron badge.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelift shown at the October 2024 Paris show: headlights moved up, new front and rear panels and the new Citroën logo; technical data unchanged.

models.name: C-Zero
models.description: Four-seat city car rebadged from the Mitsubishi i-MiEV and built by Mitsubishi in Japan for PSA, sold in Europe from late 2010 until 2020. Its twin was the Peugeot iOn; Citroën replaced it with the Ami.

generations.name: C-Zero
generations.description: Mitsubishi i-MiEV based; the PSA cars switched to an 80-cell 14.5 kWh pack from model year 2013.

models.name: E-Méhari
models.description: Open four-seat electric leisure car with a fabric roof, based on the Bolloré Bluesummer and built in Rennes from 2016 to 2019 (about 1,000 made). It used a 30 kWh lithium-metal-polymer battery and a 50 kW motor.

generations.name: E-Méhari
generations.description: Bolloré Bluesummer based; NEDC urban range 200 km.

models.name: ë-C3
models.description: Low-cost B-segment electric car on Stellantis' Smart Car platform, built in Trnava (Slovakia) and Kragujevac (Serbia) since 2024. It uses LFP batteries: 44 kWh from launch and a cheaper 30 kWh Urban Range from 2025.

generations.name: Fourth generation C3
generations.description: Introduced in October 2023, deliveries from 2024; shares its body with the petrol and hybrid C3.

models.name: ë-C3 (India)
models.description: Electric version of the low-cost C3 built in Tiruvallur, India for India and other emerging markets; it is unrelated to the European ë-C3. Launched in India on 27 February 2023 with a 29.2 kWh battery and a 42 kW motor; also sold in Indonesia from 2024.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Smart Car platform hatchback; Global NCAP gave it 0 stars for adults in 2024.

models.name: ë-C3 Aircross
models.description: Electric version of the second-generation European C3 Aircross, a B-SUV on the Smart Car platform built in Trnava since 2024, available with five or seven seats. A 54 kWh extended-range battery joined the 44 kWh version in 2025.

models.name: ë-C4
models.description: Electric version of the third-generation C4, a raised hatchback on the eCMP platform built in Madrid, launched in 2020 with a 50 kWh battery. A 54 kWh / 156 hp version was added in 2023 and the car was facelifted in late 2024.

generations.name: Third generation C4
generations.description: Revealed 16 June 2020; 50 kWh battery and 100 kW motor, 54 kWh / 115 kW from mid-2023.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Unveiled at the 2024 Paris show with the Oli-inspired front, new logo, new rear lights and new seats; same two powertrains.

models.name: ë-C4 X
models.description: Fastback saloon version of the C4, unveiled on 29 June 2022; in several markets (UK, Benelux, Germany) it was first sold only as the electric ë-C4 X. It shares the ë-C4 powertrains and was facelifted with it in late 2024.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launched late 2022 with the 50 kWh / 100 kW powertrain; 54 kWh / 115 kW added in 2023.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Late-2024 facelift with the new Citroën face and logo.

models.name: ë-C5 Aircross
models.description: Electric version of the second-generation C5 Aircross, a compact SUV on the STLA Medium platform unveiled on 29 April 2025 and built in Rennes from October 2025. It is the first C5 Aircross offered as a battery-electric car, with 73 kWh and 97 kWh batteries.

generations.name: Second generation C5 Aircross
generations.description: STLA Medium platform; 160 kW DC charging.

models.name: ë-Berlingo
models.description: Electric version of the third-generation Berlingo leisure MPV (M five-seat and XL seven-seat bodies), sold from 2021. The 2024 facelift brought a new 50 kWh pack with more range. Twins: Peugeot e-Rifter, Opel/Vauxhall Combo Electric (and Toyota Proace City Verso Electric).

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: March 2024 facelift with new front and a revised 50 kWh battery giving roughly 340 km WLTP.

models.name: ë-Berlingo Multispace
models.description: Electric version of the second-generation Berlingo Multispace leisure MPV, sold in small numbers from 2017 to early 2020 with a 22.5 kWh battery.

generations.name: Second generation Berlingo
generations.description: Small-battery conversion of the second-generation Berlingo.

models.name: ë-SpaceTourer
models.description: Electric version of the SpaceTourer people carrier (Jumpy-based, up to nine seats) sold from late 2020 with 50 kWh or 75 kWh batteries and a 100 kW motor. Facelifted in 2024; twins are the Peugeot e-Traveller and Opel/Vauxhall Zafira Electric (Vivaro Life Electric in the UK).

generations.name: Original
generations.description: EMP2-based van with 50 kWh and 75 kWh packs.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: 2024 facelift with the new Citroën face; the 50 kWh version left the range in 2025.

legacy_notes.note: Legacy "ë-C4 Electric" is the 2020-2024 50 kWh / 100 kW version. Its epa_range 217 is the 350 km WLTP figure converted to miles and mislabelled EPA (the car was never sold in the US); current_price 40227 has no currency or basis; dates are malformed ("2021-15-02", "string").

Legacy Ami row: epa_range 47 is the 75 km WMTC range converted to miles (not EPA); acceleration_0_60 9.2 s and the 116 torque/136 power style values are copied from other rows and impossible for a 6 kW, 45 km/h quadricycle; battery (5.5 kWh) missing. Mapped to the original 2020-2024 Ami; a facelift went on sale in 2025.

Legacy ë-C4 X row copies the ë-C4 values (217 "EPA" miles, 136 hp, 9.2 s); the ë-C4 X was only unveiled in June 2022. Mapped to the 2022 50 kWh / 100 kW version; the model was facelifted in late 2024 and a 54 kWh version exists.

gaps: No WLTP range sourced for the ë-SpaceTourer (only EV Database real-world figures); Peugeot e-Traveller WLTP figures are on its own entry.
Ami / C-Zero / E-Méhari ranges are on WMTC or NEDC cycles, which the schema does not accept, so range is null (Ami 75 km WMTC; C-Zero 150 km NEDC; E-Méhari 200 km NEDC urban).
Ami price not sourced (no maker price page could be fetched; web search budget was exhausted during this run).
India ë-C3 price and current (2026) Indian status not verified beyond Wikipedia listing it as in production.
Commercial ë-Jumpy / ë-Jumper / ë-Berlingo Van and ë-Jumpy Combi are not included (cargo and fleet people-carrier versions).
EU prices are German list prices incl. VAT from EV Database (Nov 2026 snapshot); UK prices likewise from EV Database.
